title: Find, reach and qualify the right prospects

say: Find, reach and qualify the right prospects.
This is the video for Module 2 of Client Acquisition Basics.
This module is the engine of client acquisition. First, you build a list of 30 real, researched prospects.

say: Then you write short, personal messages that people actually reply to.

say: And you hold short qualifying calls that tell you quickly who is worth a proposal.

say: A prospect is not a category like 'schools'. It is a named business, a named contact, and one thing you noticed. Thirty researched prospects are worth more than three hundred copied numbers.
Start with 20 warm contacts who know you, then add businesses from Google Maps, social media and directories.

panel.heading: What to record for each prospect
items: Where you found them, how to reach them

say: In a simple sheet, write the business name and location, and the contact person and role.

panel.heading: What to record for each prospect
items: Where you found them, how to reach them

say: Note where you found them and how to reach them.

panel.heading: What to record for each prospect
items: Where you found them, how to reach them

say: Write one specific observation, such as 'menu photos are blurry'. This is what makes your message personal.

panel.heading: What to record for each prospect
items: Where you found them, how to reach them

say: Then give a score. One point each for clear need, can pay, and a decider you can reach. Contact the 3s first.

items: Where you found them, how to reach them

say: Only record business details the business itself made public, or that someone gave you with permission.

panel.heading: Respect people's contact details
items: Use details the business made public
Never copy numbers from private groups
Delete anyone who asks you to stop

say: Do not copy members' numbers from private WhatsApp groups to message them for business.

say: Keep your sheet private, and delete people who ask you to stop contacting you. The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 expects personal data to be used fairly.

say: And never add strangers to a broadcast list. WhatsApp can restrict accounts that many people block or report.

panel.rule: One personal message, never a copy-pasted blast.

say: A message like 'I do graphic design, let me know if you need anything' is easy to ignore, because it asks the reader to do the thinking. A good message has four parts, under about 100 words.

panel.heading: The four-part message
items: One small ask with a yes or no answer

say: A personal opening. Greet her by name, and say who referred you.

panel.heading: The four-part message
items: One small ask with a yes or no answer

say: One observation that shows you looked. For example, 'I saw your new branch opens next month.'

panel.heading: The four-part message
items: One small ask with a yes or no answer

say: A useful offer. Connect your service to her situation, with a result she cares about.

panel.heading: The four-part message
items: One small ask with a yes or no answer

say: And one small ask. Not 'can we sign a contract', but 'would a 10-minute call on Thursday work?' A small yes moves her into a conversation.

panel.heading: The four-part message
items: One small ask with a yes or no answer

say: For example, Chioma, a designer, first wrote: 'I do logos, flyers, menus and more. Contact me if you need anything.' It gives the owner no reason to reply.

panel.heading: Chioma rewrites a weak message
right: Clear on phones, saves staff time

say: Her new message greets Mr Tamuno by name, notes that his menu photo is hard to read on a phone, explains that a clear menu saves staff time, and offers a quick mock-up with no obligation.
Just 74 words. Send 2 to 3 messages like this each weekday, during working hours.

panel.heading: Chioma rewrites a weak message
right: Clear on phones, saves staff time

say: When someone replies with interest, do not rush to send a price. Hold a short qualifying call first, using a checklist called BANT.

panel.heading: BANT: four things to find out

say: Budget. Ask gently, 'Have you set aside a budget, or would it help if I shared typical ranges?'

panel.heading: BANT: four things to find out

say: Authority. 'Apart from you, who else will be involved in deciding?'

panel.heading: BANT: four things to find out

say: Need. 'What is happening now that made you interested?' Listen more than you talk, and write down her exact words.

panel.heading: BANT: four things to find out

say: Timeline. 'When would you like this in place?' If you cannot tick at least need and authority, you are not ready to propose.

panel.heading: BANT: four things to find out

say: For example, Halima learned that a school wanted more enquiries within 6 weeks, and that the administrator could approve a small trial himself. So she proposed the trial.

cards.d: Need and authority are clear, and budget and timing are close.
A real need, but the timing is months away. Note a follow-up date.
No real need or no way to pay. Letting go frees your time.

say: Nurture when the need is real but the timing is months away. Send something useful now and then.

cards.d: Need and authority are clear, and budget and timing are close.

say: And let go politely when there is no need or no way to pay. That is not failure. If the budget is small, offer a smaller scope instead of cutting your fee.

say: So remember. Research before you write. Keep messages short with one small ask.
On calls, the common mistakes are talking about yourself first, giving a firm price too early, and ending with 'I will get back to you' and no date.

panel.heading: Key points from Module 2
items: A named business, contact and observation
Do not talk about yourself first
No firm price before you know the scope
Always agree a next step and date
